raw_response:
I've been farming this land my whole life, same as my father before me. Here in Quzhou, there's really only one system that makes sense: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same ground. That's what everyone does, that's what the land is suited for, and I know how to do it well. I have 12 mu of contracted land.

For wheat, I'll plant in mid-October after preparing the ground with the rotary tiller. I'll buy the improved variety from the county seed shop — probably Jimai 22, it's reliable and the buyers know it. Before planting I'll apply compound fertilizer as my base, then topdress with urea at jointing stage. I water at sowing, then again before winter sets in, then at jointing, then at heading. Four irrigations is what I've always done. I'll spray once or twice — once for weeds early on, once for aphids and powdery mildew near heading.

Right after wheat harvest in June, I'll direct-seed maize into the stubble — no need to plow, saves time and money. Zhengdan 958 is what I use, good stable hybrid. I'll apply urea twice: once at the seedling stage, once at big bell. Maize usually gets enough rain in summer but I'll irrigate if it gets dry in July. Spray for corn borer once, maybe aphids too if bad.
